body.p: This paper is submitted with respect to the Office Action mailed on 27 November 2024. Claims 1, 3, 4, 7, 13-18, and 20 are amended. No new matter has been added. There are no new claims. Therefore, claims 1-20 are pending.

Examiner Leung, Primary Examiner Zarroli and the undersigned held a brief telephone discussion on 31 January 2025. Among other things, proposed claim amendments to independent claim 1 were presented and discussed. Agreement was reached that the presented claim amendments to claim 1 appear to overcome all pending rejections, i.e. the 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) and 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) rejections, and the objection of the drawings under 37 C.F.R. @ 1.83(a). However, no agreement was reached regarding allowance of any claims because a new prior art search is required. The undersigned thanks Examiner Leung and Primary Examiner Zarroli for their time and guidance.

p.u: Objection to the Drawings under 37 C.F.R.

body.p: The drawings are objected to under 37 C.F.R. @ 1.83(a) because the drawings are

asserted to not show the recited thrusters feature of "configured to provide 6 DOE thruster firing." Without admission as to the validity of the objection and solely to facilitate prosecution, the feature at issue has been deleted from each of independent claims 1, 13, and 14 and thus the objection is moot. Therefore, the drawing objections being addressed, Applicant requests the drawing objections be withdrawn.

Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) and under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) for failing to comply with the written description requirement and as being indefinite, respectively, with reference to the thruster feature "configured to provide 6 DOE thruster firing."

Without admission as to the validity of the § 112(a) and § 112(b) rejections and solely to facilitate prosecution, the feature at issue has been deleted from each of independent claims 1, 13, and 14 and therefore the rejections are moot.
Therefore, the rejections being addressed, Applicant requests the § 112(a) and § 112(b) rejections be withdrawn.

p.u: Independent Claim 1 Amendments with respect to Examiner Interview

body.p: Claim 1 is presented with the features presented during the Examiner Interview and therefore overcomes, per agreement, the pending set of 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) and 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) rejections and the objection of the drawings under 37 C.F.R. § 1.83(a). Therefore, independent claim 1 is allowable. Claims 2-6 and 8-12, depending from allowable claim 1, are therefore also allowable.

p.u: Further Claim Amendments to Independent Claim 1

body.p: Independent claim 1 has been further amended solely to facilitate prosecution and to further distinguish claim 1 from the prior art, to include, e.g., U.S. Pat. Publ. No. 2021/0078732 to Reitman ("Reitman"). Specifically, claim 1 recites, inter alia, the feature:
the controller further configured with commands to fire the first thruster and the second thruster to follow a rendezvous trajectory that matches orbital parameters of the servicer
satellite and the client satellite

This feature, at least, is not disclosed nor suggested by Reitman or any other prior art. Reitman, e.g., describes station keeping operations of a servicer satellite docked with a client satellite, and is silent regarding the rendezvous structure of a servicer satellite as recited in claim 1, to include the above feature.
Thus, this feature provides a further distinction to the prior art and provides further evidence that claim 1, and its dependent claims 2-6 and 8-12, are allowable.

In addition to deleting the thruster feature "configured to provide 6 DOF thruster firing" as described above, independent claim 13 has been amended solely to facilitate prosecution and to further distinguish claim 13 from the prior art, to include, e.g., Reitman. Specifically, claim 13 recites, inter alia, the features1:
a controller configured with commands to:
... fire the first thruster and the second thruster to follow a rendezvous trajectory that matches
orbital parameters of the servicer satellite and the client satellite; and
a controller configured with commands to:
... fire the first thruster and the second thruster to accelerate the servicer satellite toward the
client satellite

These features, at least, are not disclosed nor suggested by Reitman or other prior art. Reitman, e.g., describes station keeping operations of a servicer satellite docked with a client satellite, and is silent regarding the servicer satellite structure as recited in claim 13, to include the above features.
Thus, such features provide further distinctions to the prior art and evidence that claim 13 and its dependent claim 7 are allowable.

In addition to deleting the thruster feature "configured to provide 6 DOF thruster firing" as described above, independent claim 14 has been amended solely to facilitate prosecution and to further distinguish claim 14 from the prior art, to include, e.g., Reitman. Specifically, claim 14 recites, inter alia, the feature:
the controller fires the first thruster and the second thruster to follow a first rendezvous
trajectory that matches orbital parameters of the servicer satellite and the client satellite

1 The second highlighted feature finds support at least at pg. 25, 11. 14-26 of the application as filed, i.e., "Generally, the RvD phase of operation comprises thrusting along the positive Z axis for steering the LEXI toward the host satellite. An on-board satellite computer using on-board sensors computes the thrust profile (acceleration and deceleration) for the LEXI to execute. ... The two diagonal thrusters (for example Ni and S2) are fired continuously based on a trajectory profile calculated by the LEXI on board computer and guidance and control system. As long as the acceleration is needed, the two diagonal thrusters are operating and close the range between the LEXI and the Host satellite. In case the trajectory calls for deceleration or reaching a complete stop of the acceleration or producing an outer plane corrections in the X or Y directions, the two diagonal thrusters (for example Ni and S2) in the positive Z direction are turned off. Two other diagonal thrusters (for example N2 and Si) are used such that the thruster vector is in the negative Z direction for decelerating the LEXI.
This feature, at least, is not disclosed nor suggested by Reitman or other prior art.

Reitman, e.g., describes station keeping operations of a servicer satellite docked with a client satellite, and is silent regarding the rendezvous operations of a servicer satellite as recited in claim 14, to include the above feature.
Thus, this feature provides a further distinction to the prior art and provides further evidence that claim 14, and its dependent claims 15-20, are allowable.

The Applicant thanks the Examiner for the thorough review of the application. The Applicant respectfully submits the present application, as amended, is in condition for allowance and respectfully requests the issuance of a Notice of Allowability as soon as practicable. In the event that a telephone conversation would further prosecution and/or expedite allowance, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned.
